text.p: Italy's debt markets held to firmer levels in late afternoon, but were off earlier highs, on confidence that EMU would start on time after EU finance ministers reached a stability pact and jobs accord in Amsterdam.

Dealers said that the EMU optimism had boosted higher yielding bonds like Italy and Spain as Monday's Amsterdam deal was seen to have boosted Italy's chances of joining EMU from its scheduled start at the beginning of 1999.
"Sentiment is positive after Amsterdam, but we were bound to see some profit taking at these high levels," said one trader on the LIFFE market.
